strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clear articulation of the distinction between surface-level conceptual recombination and motivation-grounded reasoning, with compelling critique of pure external scaffolding approaches

Thoughtful composite reward design: Entropy-aware information gain (EAIG) targets technical depth while contrastive semantic gain (CSG) ensures conceptual alignment; the synergy effectively balances micro-level and macro-level objectives

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple strong baselines, retrieval-augmented LLM judge validated against human experts (r=0.715, p<0.001), extensive ablations demonstrating that improvements come from learning patterns not reward hacking

Strong qualitative analysis: Training dynamics visualizations clearly show the model learns robust reasoning rather than exploiting shortcuts; theoretical analysis (Appendix F) of GRPO's length bias and length-anchoring mechanism is insightful
Reproducibility: Detailed appendices covering data construction, baseline adaptation, evaluation protocols, hyperparameters, and promise to release code facilitate validation
Pedagogical clarity: Qualitative examples (Appendix H) convincingly show MoRI's advantages in structured reasoning, technical coherence, and logical grounding compared to baselines
weaknesses: Severe domain limitation undermines generalizability claims: Only evaluated on ML/NLP papers from ICLR 2024-2025 with no evidence of transfer to other scientific domains (biology, physics, chemistry) with different logical structures; fundamentally limits scope of contribution from 'scientific ideation' to 'ML-paper-style ideation'

Modest improvements over direct baseline: +6.7% gain over Full-SFT (3.19 vs 2.99) is marginal given RL complexity; larger gains vs commercial models confounded by architecture/training differences, raising questions about whether RL complexity is justified

Ground truth and evaluation methodology limitations: Published papers as ground truth are curated but not validated as novel; LLM-as-judge (Gemini-2.5-Pro) has known biases; human evaluation on only 60 samples; fundamentally subjective metrics (novelty, feasibility) lack objective validation; missing user studies testing actual implementability

Synthetic reasoning chain artifacts: Posterior reconstruction synthesizes reasoning traces via LLM rewriting conditioned on ground truth, potentially creating overly constrained patterns; no validation that synthetic chains reflect actual scientific reasoning; de-symbolization removes technical signal

Limited dataset and limited analysis: Only 8,000 samples (2,000 for RL) from single venue; no dataset statistics (length, complexity, diversity) or analysis of potential ICLR biases; small by modern standards

Reward design contains arbitrary choices: 25% entropy threshold chosen empirically (only compared to 50%); piecewise step-function thresholds (Appendix C) unjustified; weight selection (w_s=0.7, w_e=0.3) empirically tuned without sensitivity analysis; frozen SFT model baseline not justified

RL training underspecified: Only 400 training steps (convergence unclear); small rollout size G=16 may have high variance; learning rate and hyperparameters not justified; no ablation of RL algorithm choice; no discussion of training instability

Baseline comparison fairness concerns: Commercial models only get chain-of-thought prompting (not fine-tuning); agentic baselines heavily adapted with unclear preservation of core properties; train/test split (8K for Full-SFT, 2K for RL) not perfectly balanced

Missing critical analyses: No failure mode analysis; no computational cost comparison; no scalability study across model sizes; no diversity metrics for generated ideas; limited analysis of motivation-generation quality
